en: III: 20, Taittirīya Upaniṣad III: 32–4: "From food, faith is born; from austerity, the sacred word (brahman) is born; from the sacred word, action is born; from action, the worlds are born; and from the worlds, the gods are born. "Food indeed is the root of all this; food is the foundation. For when one obtains food, one finds strength for the performance of sacred rites. "Those who worship austerity as brahman reach the light, attain heaven, and become immortal. But even greater than that is faith, for through faith one performs sacrifice and austerity, and by means of the sacred word, one attains immortality. 308, Viśvarūpa: "The one who has many forms, who shines with various colors, who dwells in the midst of the waters, and who has entered into every single being—him alone do I know as Brahman; I know not anything else."

III: 24. Is this Vṛddha-Viṣṇu, since Viṣṇu is cited immediately before? Some of these verses are cited in the *Smṛticandrikā* (Āśaucakāṇḍa, pp. 44–45) as being from Vṛddha-Manu and from Manu. Could "Mit" be an error for "Vṛddha-Manu"? The *Bālambhaṭṭī* (III: 76) glosses: "The word 'Vṛddha' means Manu and Pracetas."—Vṛddha-Pracetas.
